# Support — where to get help

Thanks for using Vant. Here's where each kind of question belongs, so
it reaches the right people fast.

## Ask a question / "how do I…?"

**[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/dhaupin/vant/discussions)** —
the front door for anything that isn't a confirmed bug. Q&A, ideas,
show-and-tell (what did your agents build?), and mesh war stories all
live there.

## Report a bug

**[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/dhaupin/vant/issues)** with the
bug template. The template asks for what you expected, what happened,
and steps to reproduce — that's exactly what gets a fix moving.
Vant is test-pinned software: a bug report with a reproduction usually
becomes a passing test within a few passes.

## Suggest a feature

Open a **[Discussion](https://github.com/dhaupin/vant/discussions)**
first (feature ideas get shaped there), then an issue once the idea has
a concrete shape. Big ideas are welcome — the project runs on PRDs and
waves, and yours can become one.

## Report a security vulnerability

**Do not open a public issue.** Use
[GitHub's private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/dhaupin/vant/security/advisories/new)
for anything exploitable. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how
reports are handled, credited, and fixed.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and the
[contributing guide](https://github.com/dhaupin/vant/blob/axolotl/docs/getting-started/contributing.md).
Agent contributors are first-class here — AGENTS.md is the real
interface, and every fix ships with the test that proves it.

## What to expect

Vant is developed in the open, in logged passes — failures and gaps
included. Response times are best-effort (this is an open-source
project, not a help desk), but nothing gets silently ignored: if an
issue needs triage, say so in the discussion and it gets eyes.
